coverage.assessment: The tree-climb motive is cut, leaving 'So I started up' unmotivated. Julius's departure is now caused by Tommy's silence rather than his recovered foot. Waterloo, the ticket, the wire and the car plan are all intact.
The nurse now walks to the window without the 'raining' question that prompted her. The Bournemouth hotel, villa, tree, branch and moon sequence still holds. Hall names the nursing home himself.
Tuppence's 'Go on' is cut, so two Julius speeches sit back to back with no attribution. The opening exchange of mutual ignorance is clipped. Other attributions are clear.
Julius's caveat 'if the girl was really Whittington's niece' is removed, along with his reason for not naming Whittington. Hall's literal 'Jane Finn? No.' survives exactly.
The nurse's face stays unseen and nothing hints that she is Jane. Cutting her nodding and head-shaking 'as though she were answering questions' leaves her a more passive figure.
The 'skunk'/gun outburst, 'got the hump' and Hall's 'Capital. Capital.' are lost. Plain report now carries much of the pursuit section, the risk the plan named.
Julius's distrust of Carter and of lawyers stays unexplained, so the ambiguity holds. His liking for Hall is kept, and Tuppence's trust in Sir James still stands against Julius's objection.
All local endpoints survive. Four partners are intact. The 013 revision drops 'He's got a new Rolls-Royce car', so the Rolls echo is gone on the partner side.

strengths: All seven verbatim anchors survive intact, including the shadow reveal and the crash.
Hall's literal 'Jane Finn? No.' and the Nurse Edith departure clue are kept word for word, with no hint that the nurse is Jane.
Julius's sharp objection to lawyers and his unexplained doubt about Carter stay without motive or comment, preserving the fair-play ambiguity.
Continuity holds: Wednesday parting, the unopened wire, 'Mrs. Who?', and Hall naming his private nursing home.
The Rolls-Royce purchase keeps its thirty-five-minute timing and the 'he got out' punchline.
summary: The revision keeps every essential plot beat, all seven verbatim anchors and the five local dependency endpoints. Its added cuts, mostly made after the first draft, fall on Julius's yarn. They remove the motive that leads into a surviving 'So I started up', Julius's doubt about Nurse Edith being a niece, the nurse's observed answering gestures, and Tuppence's interjection at the yarn's climax. They also thin Julius's idiom, which the plan flagged as a risk. These are editorial repairs, not blockers. The Rolls-Royce partner line has been cut in the 013 revision.
